first_impression.reaction: Googled 'getting married in seychelles' on the train. The intro gives a straight yes in the first few lines, and the Key Takeaways give me the shape of it: apostilled papers, banns or a special licence, register with both of you there, then sort the certificate before you fly. Fine. But the takeaway about the banns doesn't say how long they run. I had to scroll down to find 'eleven days'. Then I went to the FAQ to check if we can marry on the beach and still couldn't tell. Bookmarked, but the two things I'd actually ask a friend (how long and can it be on the beach) are harder to find than they should be.

journey.quote: The Seychelles is on your shortlist, and before you choose a bay or a resort you want to know one thing: will the marriage stand? It will.
journey.reaction: Yes in the first two lines. No fluff. Good.

journey.quote: Getting married in Seychelles is open to two Australians, because anyone aged 18 or over may marry under Seychelles law.
journey.reaction: Two Australians again. I'm in Singapore. It says 'anyone aged 18 or over', so I'm guessing it's me too, but the page keeps framing everything for Australians.

journey.quote: Allow for the banns period before your date, or apply for a special marriage licence if you want to marry sooner.
journey.reaction: How long is the banns period? This is the takeaway I'd screenshot and it has no number in it. The number is further down.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in the Seychelles?
journey.quote: As at November 2026, the age to marry in the Seychelles is 18 and over, for a man or a woman, and any person in accordance with the laws of Seychelles can marry.
journey.reaction: Dated, and it links to the government page. That answers my 'is this still true?' worry.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Start with the travel side, because it has its own rules and they can move.
journey.reaction: Smartraveller, Digital Travel Authorisation, yellow fever, healthcare, the High Commission in Mauritius. Five paragraphs before the document list. Mostly not for me. Scrolled.

journey.section: What the Civil Status office asks for
journey.quote: Australian documents are already in English, so for most couples the work lies in the apostille rather than the translation.
journey.reaction: Short bold list, and this line tells me where the real work is. Useful.

journey.section: The banns and a special licence
journey.quote: Before the marriage can take place, the banns are published for eleven days before the date of the wedding.
journey.reaction: There it is. Eleven days, and the licence is 'normally issued within two days'. That's the answer I came for. Should be at the top.

journey.section: Who performs the ceremony, and where
journey.quote: A fee applies when both of you are foreigners.
journey.reaction: Just tell me how much. 'A fee applies' and 'a higher rate', no numbers anywhere.

journey.quote: If you would like your marriage registered at home rather than at the office, tell the Civil Status office at least a week before the wedding takes place.
journey.reaction: 'At home'? Whose home? I'm flying in, I don't have a home there. Does this mean a hotel or a beach? I re-read it twice and I'm still not sure.

journey.quote: Ask the office and your resort together whether the beach in front of your resort can host the civil ceremony, and who arranges the officer's attendance.
journey.reaction: The question is 'Can we marry on the beach?' and the answer is 'ask them'. Not a yes, not a no. That's the one I'd most want answered.

journey.quote: The banns run for eleven days before the wedding, and a special marriage licence, normally issued within two days, can shorten that wait.
journey.reaction: Clear and direct. If I'd jumped straight to the FAQ, this would have saved me the scroll.

journey.section: Plan your Seychelles wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Sales bit, fine. 'Quotes in AUD' tells me this is an Australian company. Still no idea what anything costs.

unanswered_questions: How much is the Civil Status fee for two foreigners, and how much higher is it on other islands? (page says only 'A fee applies'; fee amount deferred)
How much does the special marriage licence cost? (page says 'a fee applies'; fee amount deferred)
Can the legal civil ceremony actually take place on a beach or at a resort, or does it have to be in the office? (FAQ says to ask the office and resort)
What does 'registered at home' mean for visitors who don't live in the Seychelles? Does it cover a hotel or beach?
Do we need witnesses, and how many? (page says to ask the office)
Does any of this change if we aren't Australian, for example coming from Singapore? The law says 'any person', but the page is framed for Australians.
Roughly what does a Seychelles wedding cost overall, and how is the Wedded Wonderland planning fee charged? (deferred business detail)
Does Wedded Wonderland earn commission from Seychelles resorts and suppliers? (deferred business detail)
Do you have anyone on the ground in the Seychelles, or is it run from Australia? (deferred business detail)
Can I see a real Seychelles wedding you've planned? (deferred business detail)
Any perks or Wedded Privileges for booking Seychelles resorts through you? (deferred business detail)
Will you handle the Civil Status paperwork, the special licence and the apostille errands after the wedding, or is that on us? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange airport, inter-island and ferry transfers, including the officer's transport to an outer island? (deferred business detail)
Do you work with couples who don't live in Australia? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Allow for the banns period before your date, or apply for a special marriage licence if you want to marry sooner.
turn_offs_found.why: The single most useful number on the page (eleven days, or about two days for a licence) is missing from the Key Takeaways. I'd read the takeaways and leave without it.

turn_offs_found.quote: Ask the office and your resort together whether the beach in front of your resort can host the civil ceremony, and who arranges the officer's attendance.
turn_offs_found.why: The FAQ heading asks 'Can we marry on the beach?' and the answer doesn't say yes or no. Combined with 'Registration is made in the office', I come away thinking maybe not, which is the opposite of the picture on the page.

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would like your marriage registered at home rather than at the office, tell the Civil Status office at least a week before the wedding takes place.
turn_offs_found.why: 'At home' makes no sense to a visitor. I can't tell if it means a hotel, a villa or a beach, and this sentence is repeated in three places as if it answers the beach question.

turn_offs_found.quote: Start with the travel side, because it has its own rules and they can move.
turn_offs_found.why: Five travel and health paragraphs sit before the document checklist. On a phone that's a lot of scrolling before the list I came for.

would_share_with: My partner: the Key Takeaways and the 'The banns and a special licence' section, as screenshots

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=getting-married-in-seychelles&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I came for the steps and got most of them. I don't know this brand, it's clearly aimed at Australians, and I'm not choosing a planner yet. Bookmark, not enquiry.

top_3_changes: Put the numbers in the Key Takeaways: banns run for eleven days, and a special licence is normally issued within two days. That's the timing answer most searchers want.

Make the beach answer plain. If the source supports it, say whether the civil ceremony can be held at a resort or on a beach; if not, say directly that the legal registration happens at the office unless the office agrees otherwise, and the beach can host the symbolic ceremony. Explain what 'registered at home' means for visitors, or reword it.

Move or shorten the 'Before you go: entry and documents' travel paragraphs so the Civil Status document list comes sooner on mobile, and add one line near the top saying the Seychelles steps apply to any two foreign visitors, with only the certificate-for-Australia section being Australia-specific.

open_questions.question: Does the source pack say whether a civil ceremony can be registered at a hotel, villa or beach (what 'registered at home' covers for visitors)? If so, the beach FAQ should give a direct answer.

assumptions: Priya arrived from a Google search for 'getting married in seychelles' on her phone, does not know the brand and is based in Singapore, so relevance is 4 (the Seychelles steps apply to foreigners generally) and enquiry likelihood is 1.
Deferred business details and fee amounts are not penalised and are listed as unanswered questions only.
The 3-minute budget covered the intro, Key Takeaways, the legal section, a skim past entry and travel, the document list, the banns, registration and ceremony sections, and the FAQ and closing CTA.
